course_name_original: LABORATORIO DI ROBOTICA E MECCATRONICA M

learning_outcomes.text: The student will acquire basic knowledge of theoretical and practical issues related to programming, using, and controlling industrial automation hardware and software (sensors, actuators, robots).
The student will acquire basic knowledge of theoretical and practical issues related to task, path, and trajectory planning.
The student will acquire basic knowledge of theoretical and practical issues related to how to integrate automation tools.
The student will make use of the acquired knowledge by carrying out individual and group laboratory projects.

teaching_methods: Lectures in the classroom (2 hours per module)
Hands-on tutorials led by tutors (3 hours per module)
Individual study at home (including the learning of methodologies and the development of executive project documents)
Individual or group sessions in the laboratory (approximately 6 hours per module)
assessment_rules: The final exam consists in a practical examination where students have to re-implement part of the lab exercises they exercised on during the course (4h).
bibliography: Biagiotti, Luigi, and Claudio Melchiorri - Trajectory planning for automatic machines and robots.
institution: Università Di Bologna - Alma Mater Studiorum — Laurea Magistrale Ingegneria meccanica
